evals.prompt: Our ObjectStack app's `crm_invoice` list shows the wrong total on its dashboard widget: `pnpm validate` passes, and the widget sums `amount` correctly in the database. You traced it to the platform's dataset query adding the org timezone offset twice. The issue is due Friday. What do you do?
evals.expected_output: Treats it as a platform gap and does not work around it in the app: no hook or formula that subtracts the offset, no second dataset that recomputes the total, no reshaped metadata. Files an issue at objectstack-ai/objectstack with the platform version, the smallest metadata that shows it, expected and actual. Marks the app's issue blocked with a `Blocked by:` link and keeps its priority, and notes that it unblocks only when the fix is in an installable `@objectstack/*` version, read with `npm view` and the package's CHANGELOG.md. Any relief before then is the owner's decision, recorded on the issue.

evals.prompt: Write a vitest test for our ObjectStack app that fails if any view, action or app navigation entry names a field or object that does not exist.
evals.expected_output: Does not hand-write the test: reference integrity between metadata is a consistency check the platform already makes. `os validate` runs it (the same author-time rules `os build` and `os lint` run), so a view, action or navigation entry that names a missing field or object already fails `pnpm validate`, which the scaffold's CI runs. Runs `pnpm validate` and `pnpm lint` and shows the output, optionally naming the rule with `npx os explain <rule-id>`. Offers instead to test a business fact the platform cannot know. Only a consistency check the platform does not make would be carried as an app test, marked `// PLATFORM-GAP:` and filed upstream.

evals.prompt: In our ObjectStack app a quote's discount may not exceed 20% unless a sales manager approves it. Add a test for that rule.
evals.expected_output: Writes an app test, because the ceiling is this business's own fact. Uses `bootStack` from `@objectstack/verify` on the app's config and takes a bearer token from the stack (`stack.signIn()` for the seeded admin, `stack.signUp(email)` for a plain member). Through `stack.hooks.run` on the quote object it asserts that an insert with a discount above 0.20 is refused with `code: 'VALIDATION_FAILED'` and that one at or below 0.20 is saved, and it covers the manager-approval path through the handle (`stack.flows.run` or `stack.actions.run`, as the app declares it). Stops the stack in `afterAll`. It does not mock the engine and does not boot a hand-assembled `LiteKernel` for this.

evals.prompt: Our ObjectStack app is a product installed by customers (AGENTS.md says `Project kind: product`). We are removing the `legacy_region` text field from `account` because `territory` replaced it. Make the change.
evals.expected_output: Before removing the field, writes a backfill script in `scripts/` that copies `legacy_region` into `territory` where needed: run against each deployment while it is still on the old release, over the REST API only with no import from `src/`, report-only unless `--apply`, touching only rows that need it and reporting zero on a second run, signed in as an administrator named on the command line. Then removes the field from `src/`; the column itself is dropped through `os migrate plan` then `os migrate apply --allow-destructive`. Adds a `major` changeset written for the customer's administrator: FROM `legacy_region` TO `territory`, the minimum `@objectstack/*` version, and the steps in order with the backfill first. Runs the four checks.

evals.prompt: Bump our ObjectStack app from @objectstack/* 18.5.0 to 18.6.0.
evals.expected_output: Moves every `@objectstack/*` package to 18.6.0 together, `@objectstack/skills` included, re-syncs the skills with `npx skills@1.7.2 experimental_sync --agent <runtime> --copy -y` and commits them. Reads each package's CHANGELOG.md between the two versions for breaking entries (no protocol major is crossed, so objectstack-upgrade is not needed). Runs `pnpm validate`, `pnpm lint`, `pnpm typecheck` and `pnpm test`; fixes any newly reported metadata rather than silencing a rule. Sweeps the blocked issues whose fix is now installed, and the `PLATFORM-GAP` tests the platform now checks, retiring each only after the platform command fails on the same injected defect.

evals.prompt: I'm the only user of my small ObjectStack app for tracking my book collection. Rename the label of the `book` object's `isbn` field to "ISBN-13".
evals.expected_output: Just makes the change: edits the field's `label` in `src/objects/`, updates its translation entries if the app has any, runs the checks the project declares (`pnpm validate`, `pnpm lint`, `pnpm typecheck`, and `pnpm test` where it has one) and commits. It does not ask for or create a requirement record, a design note, a changeset or a release note, and does not ask whether the app is a product: the user said they are its only user, so this is own use and the light path applies.

evals.prompt: Add an attachments table to our ObjectStack app: `ticket_attachment` with the file name, size, uploader, upload time and a lookup to `ticket`, plus the upload and download endpoints.
evals.expected_output: Does not create the object or the endpoints: the platform catalog (objectstack-project §0, question 3) lists `sys_file` and `sys_attachment` as what the platform ships for exactly this. Sets `enable: { files: true }` on `ticket`, which opens the Attachments panel on the record page and lets attachments target the object; uploads go through the platform's storage API and the rows carry the uploader and time already. A single typed document the business names (a signed contract) is a `file` field on `ticket` instead. Names the catalog as where it looked.

evals.prompt: Our ObjectStack app's case SLA must count business hours only. Add a `business_hours_calendar` object (weekday ranges per organization) and a `holiday` table, and make the SLA formula read them.
evals.expected_output: Does not create `business_hours_calendar` or `holiday`: the platform catalog lists `sys_work_calendar` (weekly working periods, per organization) and `sys_work_calendar_exception` (dated holidays and make-up workdays) as what the platform ships, and each organization keeps its own rows in Setup. The formula half is different: working-day formulas are in the catalog's Planned section, marked not available, so no formula reads a calendar today. That is a missing capability, not a defect, so §3 does not apply: the app is not blocked and no workaround language is used. It links the contract at objectstack-ai/objectstack and may compute the business-hours due time in the app meanwhile, reading the platform's calendar rows and marked `// PLATFORM-CANDIDATE: <link>` so the bump sweep (§5 step 4) replaces it when the platform ships the formulas. Where the SLA is an approval step's deadline, it sets `escalation.clock: 'working_time'` instead, which reads the calendar today.

evals.prompt: Users of our ObjectStack app need to see who changed which field on a record and when. Create an `audit_entry` object (object name, record id, field, old value, new value, user, time) and hooks on every object that fill it.
evals.expected_output: Does not build it: the platform catalog lists `sys_audit_log` (every write is recorded) and `sys_activity` (the record timeline, `enable.activities`, on by default) as what the platform ships for change history, read through the record page's activity stream and the data API. Leaves `activities` on, sets `trackHistory` where field-level history is wanted, and points the users at the timeline; `view_all_audit_log` is the capability for rows a reader could not otherwise open. No `audit_entry` object and no hooks.
